- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast upward; correct by reducing forecast peak by 5–15%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; reduce forecast by 3–8% for next 5–7 days.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., 0.3–0.7) and recent price is volatile; add 2–5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days below 30-day moving avg), model often fails to recognize; adjust forecast downward by 3–7% for next 5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to over-predict in early days (1–5) when sentiment is volatile; reduce forecast by 5–10% for first 3 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model often fails to anticipate downward correction; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5–7 days.
